Story & Plot

Matt Hagen rises from a Gotham street kid to a Hollywood leading man before a local crime boss leaves him horribly disfigured. Abandoned and desperate, he seeks a cutting-edge treatment that restores him to his former self while unexpectedly destroying his grip on reality. This R-rated, villain-centered horror film follows his dark, destructive spiral into all-consuming revenge.

Comedy & Entertainment

While the film is primarily a body-horror thriller rather than a comedy, reviewers note that it delivers the rollercoaster kick of laughing while your stomach begs for mercy. Its entertainment value relies heavily on B-movie absurdity, delivering a fun and gross romp that embraces its gruesome potential.

Performances & Direction

Tom Rhys Harries shines as the titular villain, leading a cast that also features Naomi Ackie, Eddie Marsan, Max Minghella, and David Dencik. Reviewers praise his work in this messy yet distinctive DC horror story. The performances anchor the sympathetic villain origin story effectively.

Strengths

  • Fun and gruesome body horror
  • Strong lead performance by Tom Rhys Harries
  • No franchise homework required
  • Effective B-movie absurdity
  • Nods to classic horror filmmakers

Weaknesses

Reviewers note that the film is underbaked and takes a while to find its groove. It can feel a bit tentative in exploring its horror territory and wants to tell a sympathetic villain origin story without fully trusting the audience to handle moral complexity.

Final verdict

Clayface is a gritty, R-rated horror throwback that gets the job done for Halloween with plenty of delicious squirms. Though it takes some time to find its groove, horror fans looking for a grotesque comic book adaptation should check it out.
